analyst_view.overall: Two struggling sides meet at the Euroborg on Friday night (20:00 local). Dick Lukkien's Groningen (10th, 15 points) have one point from their last five league games and are six without a win, the latest a 1-3 home defeat to Heerenveen in the Derby van het Noorden, which they played without banned goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen and right-back Hans Hateboer; stand-in keeper Lovro Stubljar was at fault for goals, and both regulars are available again, which the numbers can't see. Willem II are bottom with 3 points from 13 games and no league win; they lost 2-1 at Twente and wing-back Nathan Tjoe-A-On, a near-constant starter, is banned after two yellows there (the numbers already count that, along with day-to-day absences such as Hoogma and Lachkar for Willem II and Janse, Jeng and Hernes for Groningen). Groningen are unbeaten in the last five meetings (three wins, nine goals to three). Richard Martens referees, with a low card record the numbers already use; news this week stayed thin, so my only move remains a small trim to goals for Groningen's first-choice keeper and right-back returning.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, 2.8 for Groningen, and already add for Willem II's leaky defence (22 conceded in six), Groningen's own recent conceding and Tjoe-A-On's suspension. Part of Groningen's 18 conceded in six came with stand-in keeper Stubljar, and Vaessen and Hateboer are back from their bans, which the numbers can't see, so I trim slightly to about 3.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, 6.3 for Groningen. Groningen have won fewer corners than usual lately (21 in six) and the numbers already trim that, while bottom side Willem II, without Tjoe-A-On on the flank, should spend long spells defending their own box. Hateboer's return adds a right-back who gets forward, but that is too small to move, so I stay at about 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.6 cards. Richard Martens has shown about 2.8 cards a game in his four matches, below the league average of 3.1, and the numbers already count him as well as Willem II's rise in bookings (12 in six, including Tjoe-A-On's two yellows at Twente). Both clubs are under pressure but it is no derby, so I stay at about 2.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, 21.4 for Groningen. Willem II have allowed 128 shots in their last six, including a 7-0 defeat at PSV, while Groningen keep creating at home despite their results; the numbers already add that momentum (+7.5% for Groningen), so I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, 7.6 for Groningen. Groningen's shooting has been sharp (40 on target in six) and Willem II weak at the back, which the numbers already count with an 11% boost for Groningen, while Willem II themselves have managed only 15 on target in six. Nothing new points either way, so I stay at about 10.9.
